newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA SAYS WILL NOT GIVE JINNAH HOUSE TO PAKISTAN.
newsitem.headline: INDIA SAYS WILL NOT GIVE JINNAH HOUSE TO PAKISTAN.

text.p: India rebuffed Pakistan on Thursday and said it will not lease Jinnah House, a disused Bombay mansion that once was the home of Pakistan's founder Mohammed Ali Jinnah, to Islamabad.
The stately, marble-terraced building overlooking the Arabian Sea has been a bone of contention between the two nations since they were carved out of British-ruled India in 1947.
Their 50th independence anniversary falls on August 15.

"There is no question of giving Jinnah House in Mumbai (Bombay) to Pakistan for the purpose of reopening its consulate," junior Foreign Minister Kamala Sinha said in reply to a question by a lawmaker in India's upper house, Rajya Sabha.
Pakistan wants to take Jinnah House on lease as the residence of its consul-general.
"Pakistan has to acquire an accommodation if it intends to re-open its consulate in Mumbai," Sinha said.

Pakistan closed its consulate, in another Bombay building, in March 1994, saying Indian authorities were hindering its activities. India closed its consulate in Karachi in January 1995 under orders from Islamabad.
Jinnah, a brilliant lawyer, led the campaign for the formation of Islamic Pakistan, which has fought three wars with secular but largely Hindu India.
Two of the wars have been over India's Moslem-majority Kashmir region, which is claimed by Islamabad.
India offered Jinnah House to Pakistan for use as its consulate in 1977, but backed out after a sharp public outcry.
Jinnah House is currently held by the Indian Council of Cultural Relations (ICCR), a government body.

The Indian government took over the building as "evacuee property" in 1949, and the British deputy high commission occupied the house from 1948 until 1982 in accordance with the wishes of Jinnah, who died in 1948.
The building, near the residence of the chief minister of Maharashtra state, is also claimed by Jinnah's only child, Dina Wadia, 78, who lives in New York.
